#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce m2c on `chase_f` — benchmark function af:chase_f:ido7.1.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit ad5c529:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout ad5c529a65ca1e5191b00a4a7b4cbfe79a7b45a0
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'
# asmlift checkout — this function's context is the project's own vendored preprocessor
# output, stored in the repo (referenced rather than embedded — it can be hundreds of KB):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel chase_f
    mtc1	$a1, $f14
    mtc1	$a2, $f12
    mtc1	$zero, $f4
    nop
    c.eq.s	$f12, $f4
    nop
    bc1tl	.L70
    lwc1	$f4, 0($a0)
    lwc1	$f0, 0($a0)
    li	$v0, 1
    c.lt.s	$f14, $f0
    nop
    bc1fl	.L40
    add.s	$f6, $f0, $f12
    neg.s	$f12, $f12
    add.s	$f6, $f0, $f12
.L40:
    mtc1	$zero, $f18
    swc1	$f6, 0($a0)
    lwc1	$f8, 0($a0)
    sub.s	$f10, $f8, $f14
    mul.s	$f16, $f10, $f12
    c.le.s	$f18, $f16
    nop
    bc1fl	.L8c
    move	$v0, $zero
    jr	$ra
    swc1	$f14, 0($a0)
    lwc1	$f4, 0($a0)
.L70:
    c.eq.s	$f14, $f4
    nop
    bc1fl	.L8c
    move	$v0, $zero
    jr	$ra
    li	$v0, 1
    move	$v0, $zero
.L8c:
    jr	$ra
    nop
ASM_INPUT

# The project context the benchmark passed via --context: the VERBATIM vendored blob — this
# function's translation unit run through the project's own preprocessor with the function body
# removed, i.e. whatever that TU's headers and the manifest's prependC declare, and nothing
# added. How much that is varies by project (a full header tree for some, a handful of typedefs
# for others); the file below is the exact bytes, so read it rather than this comment.
gunzip -kc "$ASMLIFT_PATH/apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/af/ctx-81de3b7c6bd9.i.gz" > ctx.h

args=(
  --target mips-ido-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function chase_f      # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the project context header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

# rebuild the project itself:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce m2c on `mem_copy` — benchmark function af:mem_copy:ido7.1.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit ad5c529:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout ad5c529a65ca1e5191b00a4a7b4cbfe79a7b45a0
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'
# asmlift checkout — this function's context is the project's own vendored preprocessor
# output, stored in the repo (referenced rather than embedded — it can be hundreds of KB):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel mem_copy
    beqz	$a2, .L64
    andi	$v1, $a2, 0x3
    negu	$v1, $v1
    beqz	$v1, .L34
    addu	$v0, $v1, $a2
.L14:
    lbu	$t6, 0($a1)
    addiu	$a2, $a2, -1
    addiu	$a1, $a1, 1
    addiu	$a0, $a0, 1
    bne	$v0, $a2, .L14
    sb	$t6, -1($a0)
    beqz	$a2, .L64
    nop
.L34:
    lbu	$t7, 0($a1)
    addiu	$a2, $a2, -4
    addiu	$a1, $a1, 4
    sb	$t7, 0($a0)
    lbu	$t8, -3($a1)
    addiu	$a0, $a0, 4
    sb	$t8, -3($a0)
    lbu	$t9, -2($a1)
    sb	$t9, -2($a0)
    lbu	$t0, -1($a1)
    bnez	$a2, .L34
    sb	$t0, -1($a0)
.L64:

    nop
    nop

# The project context the benchmark passed via --context: the VERBATIM vendored blob — this
# function's translation unit run through the project's own preprocessor with the function body
# removed, i.e. whatever that TU's headers and the manifest's prependC declare, and nothing
# added. How much that is varies by project (a full header tree for some, a handful of typedefs
# for others); the file below is the exact bytes, so read it rather than this comment.
# One line is appended: the function's own prototype, and ONLY because the project's headers do
# not declare it and the row's asmlift `--proto` already carries the same void-ness. It is
# derived from that field, never from the reference source.
gunzip -kc "$ASMLIFT_PATH/apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/af/ctx-ca2382fd2e82.i.gz" > ctx.h
cat >> ctx.h <<'CTX_PROTO'
void mem_copy();
CTX_PROTO

  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

# rebuild the project itself:

#   sha256 of the decompressed map JSON: a34eefa8a123dabff0aaa822beec15fb2b928c41b91b9fe07558c6021ab587de

# step 1 then points the scoring config at the checkout's decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.elf) —
# the CLI loads the same map, so this run reproduces the row's named spellings. A missing

# CANDIDATE. So this reproduces the row; it does not reproduce a CHANGED asmlift, whose new
# candidate may name a project type this rung does not declare. See docs/ranked-repro.md,
# "What this vehicle does NOT reproduce".)
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target ido7.1         # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)

  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)

# rebuild the project itself:

# Reproduce m2c on `HuMemUsedMemoryBlockGet` — benchmark function marioparty3:HuMemUsedMemoryBlockGet:gcc2.7.2.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit ad5c529:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout ad5c529a65ca1e5191b00a4a7b4cbfe79a7b45a0
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'
# asmlift checkout — this function's context is the project's own vendored preprocessor
# output, stored in the repo (referenced rather than embedded — it can be hundreds of KB):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel HuMemUsedMemoryBlockGet
    move	$v1, $a0
    move	$a1, $zero
.L8:
    lbu	$v0, 5($v1)
    xori	$v0, $v0, 0x1
    sltiu	$v0, $v0, 1
    lw	$v1, 12($v1)
    bne	$v1, $a0, .L8
    addu	$a1, $a1, $v0
    jr	$ra
    move	$v0, $a1
ASM_INPUT

# The project context the benchmark passed via --context: the VERBATIM vendored blob — this
# function's translation unit run through the project's own preprocessor with the function body
# removed, i.e. whatever that TU's headers and the manifest's prependC declare, and nothing
# added. How much that is varies by project (a full header tree for some, a handful of typedefs
# for others); the file below is the exact bytes, so read it rather than this comment.
gunzip -kc "$ASMLIFT_PATH/apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/marioparty3/ctx-0eb9f921480c.i.gz" > ctx.h

args=(
  --target mips-gcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function HuMemUsedMemoryBlockGet # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the project context header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

# Reproduce asmlift on `MathUtil_Div16` — benchmark function pokeemerald:MathUtil_Div16:agbcc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# This function's decomp project — the PINNED benchmark branch (provenance base + one
# integration commit). Not needed to run this script (inputs are embedded/vendored); to
# rebuild the project itself:
#   git clone --branch asmlift-benchmark https://github.com/macabeus/pokeemerald.git pokeemerald
#   make -C pokeemerald
#   make -C pokeemerald asmlift-elf   # derive the symbols ELF (DWARF types-sidecar)
# SYMBOLS: this row ran WITH the project's symbol map (names + declaration shapes derived
# from the ELF its decomp.yaml names), vendored at apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/pokeemerald/symbols.json.gz
#   sha256 of the decompressed map JSON: 642d005a3a212cb1552e8e3015b474b6ffc36606a67950c6e770ece66893e819
# Set PROJECT_PATH to your BUILT checkout of the project above (clone recipe in the comments);
# step 1 then points the scoring config at the checkout's decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.elf) —
# the CLI loads the same map, so this run reproduces the row's named spellings. A missing
# checkout/ELF warns and runs map-less (output may then differ from the row).
PROJECT_PATH='/path/to/pokeemerald'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# the flags of this function's unit, copied from the project's build.
# --project-root grafts the checkout's tools.asmlift.elf (the symbol map) into that decomp.yaml.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target pokeemerald:MathUtil_Div16:agbcc --out "$PWD" --project-root "$PROJECT_PATH" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────
# The exact agbcc `.s` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'
@ Generated by gcc 2.9-arm-000512 for Thumb/elf
	.code	16
.gcc2_compiled.:
.text
	.align	2, 0
	.globl	MathUtil_Div16
	.type	 MathUtil_Div16,function
	.thumb_func
MathUtil_Div16:
.LFB1:
.LM1:

	push	{lr}
	lsl	r0, r0, #0x10
	lsr	r0, r0, #0x10
.LM2:

	lsl	r1, r1, #0x10
	asr	r1, r1, #0x10
	cmp	r1, #0
	beq	.L3	@cond_branch
.LM3:

	lsl	r0, r0, #0x10
	asr	r0, r0, #0x8
	bl	__divsi3
	lsl	r0, r0, #0x10
	asr	r0, r0, #0x10
	b	.L4
.L3:
.LM4:

	mov	r0, #0x0
.L4:
.LM5:

	pop	{r1}
	bx	r1
.LFE1:
.Lfe1:
	.size	 MathUtil_Div16,.Lfe1-MathUtil_Div16

	.section	.text
.Letext0:

.text
	.align	2, 0
ASM_INPUT

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
# (real tier: candidates are scored INSIDE a project context — step 1 materializes ONE rung of
# the benchmark's escalation ladder next to target.o as ctx.i, and the generated decomp.yaml
# concatenates it ahead of every candidate. That rung is the one THIS ROW'S PUBLISHED SOURCE
# stops at — the richest rung on a row asmlift declined — while the harness escalates PER
# CANDIDATE. So this reproduces the row; it does not reproduce a CHANGED asmlift, whose new
# candidate may name a project type this rung does not declare. See docs/ranked-repro.md,
# "What this vehicle does NOT reproduce".)
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target agbcc          # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name MathUtil_Div16   # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"

flagsFrom.command: arm-none-eabi-cpp -iquote include -Wno-trigraphs -DMODERN=0 -I tools/agbcc/include -I tools/agbcc -nostdinc -undef -std=gnu89 src/math_util.c | tools/preproc/preproc -i src/math_util.c charmap.txt | tools/agbcc/bin/agbcc -mthumb-interwork -Wimplicit -Wparentheses -Werror -O2 -fhex-asm -g -o - - | cat - <(echo -e ".text\n\t.align\t2, 0") | arm-none-eabi-as -mcpu=arm7tdmi --defsym MODERN=0 -o build/emerald/src/math_util.o -

# rebuild the project itself:

#   sha256 of the decompressed map JSON: 6ef97c7ca854fc4956f747c12dd400f3ab20cf65c31c10cca7982793726c3f3c

# Reproduce asmlift on `func_800B0DC0_1DCF60` — benchmark function snowboardkids2:func_800B0DC0_1DCF60:gcc2.7.2kmc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# This function's decomp project — the PINNED benchmark branch (provenance base + one
# integration commit). Not needed to run this script (inputs are embedded/vendored); to
# rebuild the project itself:
#   git clone --branch asmlift-benchmark https://github.com/macabeus/snowboardkids2-decomp.git snowboardkids2-decomp
#   make -C snowboardkids2-decomp
#   make -C snowboardkids2-decomp asmlift-elf   # derive the symbols ELF (DWARF types-sidecar)
# SYMBOLS: this row ran WITH the project's symbol map (names + declaration shapes derived
# from the ELF its decomp.yaml names), vendored at apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/snowboardkids2/symbols.json.gz
#   sha256 of the decompressed map JSON: 4257ee48404306f80e9cdb5dcbf5e095d27fc057335a09f2747956e79c76732e
# Set PROJECT_PATH to your BUILT checkout of the project above (clone recipe in the comments);
# step 1 then points the scoring config at the checkout's decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.elf) —
# the CLI loads the same map, so this run reproduces the row's named spellings. A missing
# checkout/ELF warns and runs map-less (output may then differ from the row).
PROJECT_PATH='/path/to/snowboardkids2-decomp'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# the flags of this function's unit, copied from the project's build.
# --project-root grafts the checkout's tools.asmlift.elf (the symbol map) into that decomp.yaml.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target snowboardkids2:func_800B0DC0_1DCF60:gcc2.7.2kmc --out "$PWD" --project-root "$PROJECT_PATH" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────
# The exact `objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'

target.o:     file format elf32-tradbigmips


Disassembly of section .text:

00000000 <func_800B0DC0_1DCF60>:
   0:	lw	v0,4(a0)
   4:	addu	v0,v0,a0
   8:	jr	ra
   c:	lw	v0,0(v0)
ASM_INPUT

# constants) the text-only disassembly lacks; the benchmark recovered them from the object.
cat > dump.txt <<'DUMP_INPUT'

target.o:     file format elf32-tradbigmips

SYMBOL TABLE:
00000000 l    df *ABS*	00000000 /host-tmp/bench-real-gcc-c4ba86b480420893/u.i

Contents of section .note:

Contents of section .comment:
 0000 00474343 3a202847 4e552920 322e372e  .GCC: (GNU) 2.7.
 0010 3200                                 2.

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
# (real tier: candidates are scored INSIDE a project context — step 1 materializes ONE rung of
# the benchmark's escalation ladder next to target.o as ctx.i, and the generated decomp.yaml
# concatenates it ahead of every candidate. That rung is the one THIS ROW'S PUBLISHED SOURCE
# stops at — the richest rung on a row asmlift declined — while the harness escalates PER
# CANDIDATE. So this reproduces the row; it does not reproduce a CHANGED asmlift, whose new
# candidate may name a project type this rung does not declare. See docs/ranked-repro.md,
# "What this vehicle does NOT reproduce".)
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target gcc2.7.2kmc    # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name func_800B0DC0_1DCF60 # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --asm-data dump.txt     # the data sections above (jump-table/const recovery)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact

# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.

# Reproduce m2c on `dmaback` — benchmark function synthetic:dmaback:agbcc.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit ad5c529:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout ad5c529a65ca1e5191b00a4a7b4cbfe79a7b45a0
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The exact agbcc `.s` text the benchmark fed m2c, verbatim.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
@ Generated by gcc 2.9-arm-000512 for Thumb/elf
	.code	16
.gcc2_compiled.:
.text
	.align	2, 0
	.globl	dmaback
	.type	 dmaback,function
	.thumb_func
dmaback:
	push	{r4, r5, r6, r7, lr}
	mov	r7, r8
	push	{r7}
	add	sp, sp, #-0x4
	add	r2, r0, #0
	cmp	r2, #0x1f
	bgt	.L4	@cond_branch
	mov	r5, sp
	mov	r0, #0x0
	mov	r8, r0
	ldr	r0, .L8
	mov	ip, r0
	ldr	r7, .L8+0x4
	lsl	r0, r1, #0x3
	ldr	r1, .L8+0x8
	add	r4, r0, r1
	ldr	r3, .L8+0xc
	ldr	r6, .L8+0x10
.L6:
	mov	r0, r8
	strh	r0, [r5]
	mov	r1, sp
	mov	r0, ip
	str	r1, [r0]
	lsl	r0, r2, #0x6
	ldr	r1, [r4, #0x4]
	add	r1, r1, r0
	str	r1, [r7]
	str	r6, [r3]
	ldr	r0, [r3]
	add	r2, r2, #0x1
	cmp	r2, #0x1f
	ble	.L6	@cond_branch
.L4:
	add	sp, sp, #0x4
	pop	{r3}
	mov	r8, r3
	pop	{r4, r5, r6, r7}
	pop	{r0}
	bx	r0
.L9:
	.align	2, 0
.L8:
	.word	0x40000d4
	.word	0x40000d8
	.word	0x3003430
	.word	0x40000dc
	.word	-0x7effffe0
.Lfe1:
	.size	 dmaback,.Lfe1-dmaback
ASM_INPUT

# The exact context header the benchmark passed via --context.
# Prototypes only — no struct or global layouts. The synthetic tier measures COLD recovery and is
# symmetric by construction: these are the same facts asmlift is given as --proto hints, and
# neither tool is given a project.
cat > ctx.h <<'CTX_INPUT'
void dmaback(s32 lo, s32 bg);
CTX_INPUT

args=(
  --target gba            # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function dmaback      # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the prototype header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `dmaback` — benchmark function synthetic:dmaback:agbcc.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# agbcc's canonical flags.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:dmaback:agbcc --out "$PWD" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────
# The exact agbcc `.s` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'
@ Generated by gcc 2.9-arm-000512 for Thumb/elf
	.code	16
.gcc2_compiled.:
.text
	.align	2, 0
	.globl	dmaback
	.type	 dmaback,function
	.thumb_func
dmaback:
	push	{r4, r5, r6, r7, lr}
	mov	r7, r8
	push	{r7}
	add	sp, sp, #-0x4
	add	r2, r0, #0
	cmp	r2, #0x1f
	bgt	.L4	@cond_branch
	mov	r5, sp
	mov	r0, #0x0
	mov	r8, r0
	ldr	r0, .L8
	mov	ip, r0
	ldr	r7, .L8+0x4
	lsl	r0, r1, #0x3
	ldr	r1, .L8+0x8
	add	r4, r0, r1
	ldr	r3, .L8+0xc
	ldr	r6, .L8+0x10
.L6:
	mov	r0, r8
	strh	r0, [r5]
	mov	r1, sp
	mov	r0, ip
	str	r1, [r0]
	lsl	r0, r2, #0x6
	ldr	r1, [r4, #0x4]
	add	r1, r1, r0
	str	r1, [r7]
	str	r6, [r3]
	ldr	r0, [r3]
	add	r2, r2, #0x1
	cmp	r2, #0x1f
	ble	.L6	@cond_branch
.L4:
	add	sp, sp, #0x4
	pop	{r3}
	mov	r8, r3
	pop	{r4, r5, r6, r7}
	pop	{r0}
	bx	r0
.L9:
	.align	2, 0
.L8:
	.word	0x40000d4
	.word	0x40000d8
	.word	0x3003430
	.word	0x40000dc
	.word	-0x7effffe0
.Lfe1:
	.size	 dmaback,.Lfe1-dmaback
ASM_INPUT

# The prototype hints the benchmark fed asmlift (callee arities / void-ness).
cat > proto.json <<'PROTO_INPUT'
{
  "dmaback": {
    "params": [
      "s32",
      "s32"
    ],
    "returnsVoid": true
  }
}
PROTO_INPUT

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target agbcc          # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name dmaback          # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --proto proto.json      # the prototype hints above (callee arities / void-ness)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.

    lbu	$t2, 2($a0)
    lbu	$a3, 3($a0)
    lbu	$t0, 4($a0)
    lbu	$t1, 5($a0)
    lbu	$t3, 6($a0)
    lbu	$t4, 7($a0)
    lbu	$t5, 8($a0)
    lbu	$t6, 1($a0)

    mult	$a3, $t0
    mflo	$v0
    mult	$t1, $t3
    mflo	$v1
    mult	$t4, $t5

results.note: the `||` at `ifand_far`'s distance. The long branch INVERTS the last test, which moves the shared arm to the other successor slot — so a long `||` stamps the same pair (`scSharedOnFall` false, `scSharedIsTaken` true) as a SHORT `&&` and wants the opposite spelling. Two booleans cannot separate them; the third stamp `scEdgeRelayed` is what does, and this is the only row whose SPELLING that stamp decides — the corpus carries 9 other stamped sites, all MIPS rows where no ±256-byte range exists and none is a sense site (packages/core/test/site-sense.test.ts pins the cell). Like `ifand_far` its SCORE referees nothing: it MATCHes on `/flip-join` whichever way the fold spelled the site. Nor does the FAN carry the variation here: measured, the row enumerates 4 candidates and no `/site-sense` at all, because at one site the variation re-spells what `/flip-join` already spelled and the tree dedup drops the duplicate. A named row the fan never enumerates is worth saying out loud

# Reproduce m2c on `llcmp` — benchmark function synthetic:llcmp:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit ad5c529:

    xoris   r7,r3,32768
    xoris   r3,r5,32768
    subfc   r0,r6,r4
    subfe   r3,r3,r7
    subfe   r3,r7,r7
    neg     r3,r3
    blr

  --function llcmp        # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run

# Reproduce m2c on `strlen1` — benchmark function synthetic:strlen1:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit ad5c529:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout ad5c529a65ca1e5191b00a4a7b4cbfe79a7b45a0
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel strlen1
    li      r4,0
    b        .L10
.L8:
    addi    r4,r4,1
    addi    r3,r3,1
.L10:
    lbz     r0,0(r3)
    extsb.  r0,r0
    bne+     .L8
    mr      r3,r4
    blr
ASM_INPUT

# (This function ran with NO context header — the benchmark fed m2c the assembly alone.)

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function strlen1      # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'

cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
@ Generated by gcc 2.9-arm-000512 for Thumb/elf
	.code	16
.gcc2_compiled.:
.text
	.align	2, 0
	.globl	sw_fallguard
	.type	 sw_fallguard,function
	.thumb_func
sw_fallguard:
	add	r2, r0, #0
	add	r0, r1, #0
	cmp	r0, #0
	bgt	.L4	@cond_branch
	cmp	r2, #0x2
	beq	.L7	@cond_branch
	cmp	r2, #0x2
	bgt	.L11	@cond_branch
	cmp	r2, #0x1
	beq	.L8	@cond_branch
	b	.L4
.L11:
	cmp	r2, #0x3
	bne	.L4	@cond_branch
	mov	r0, #0x1
.L7:
	add	r0, r0, #0x1
.L8:
	add	r0, r0, #0x1
.L4:
	bx	lr
.Lfe1:
	.size	 sw_fallguard,.Lfe1-sw_fallguard

# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# agbcc's canonical flags.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target synthetic:zxparam:agbcc --out "$PWD" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────
# The exact agbcc `.s` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'
@ Generated by gcc 2.9-arm-000512 for Thumb/elf
	.code	16
.gcc2_compiled.:
.text
	.align	2, 0
	.globl	zxparam
	.type	 zxparam,function
	.thumb_func
zxparam:
	push	{r4, lr}
	lsl	r0, r0, #0x18
	lsr	r0, r0, #0x18
	lsl	r1, r1, #0x18
	lsr	r1, r1, #0x18
	mov	r4, #0x1
	add	r3, r0, #0
	and	r3, r3, r4
	str	r3, [r2]
	add	r3, r1, #0
	and	r3, r3, r4
	str	r3, [r2, #0x4]
	add	r0, r0, r1
	str	r0, [r2, #0x8]
	pop	{r4}
	pop	{r0}
	bx	r0
.Lfe1:
	.size	 zxparam,.Lfe1-zxparam
ASM_INPUT

# The prototype hints the benchmark fed asmlift (callee arities / void-ness).
cat > proto.json <<'PROTO_INPUT'
{
  "zxparam": {
    "params": [
      "u8",
      "u8",
      "s32 *"
    ],
    "returnsVoid": true
  }
}
PROTO_INPUT

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target agbcc          # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name zxparam          # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --proto proto.json      # the prototype hints above (callee arities / void-ness)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"
